_comment: The move map IS the spec. scripts/move-tree.mjs is a pure function of this file,
and scripts/check-tree-invariants.mjs verifies totality (every tracked src file is
named here or matched by a keep rule) and injectivity (no two sources share a target).
Capability buckets come from docs/audit/03-architecture-analysis.md section 4, which
derived them from the measured dependency graph - they are adopted, not re-invented.
What changes is that each capability gets tier folders inside it, so the audit's flat
domain/ bucket becomes <capability>/domain/ and the tier is no longer a guess.
HARD RULE for batches 4-10: directories change, basenames do NOT. Exception list is
only the three batch-3 suffix fixes. This keeps git rename detection trivial so a
reviewer can verify 'same file, new folder' mechanically instead of reading diffs.
Every path below is repo-relative. 'keep' entries are framework- or platform-pinned
and moving one is either a public URL change or a contract with the app builder.

keep.src/routes/**: TanStack file-based routing: a moved route file silently changes a public URL
keep.src/routeTree.gen.ts: generated; check-tree asserts its hash never changes during the move
keep.migrations/**: discovered by two path mechanisms (import.meta.glob and readdirSync)
keep.scripts/**: repo tooling, moved only where this map says explicitly
keep.vite.config.ts: must not be recreated; only its module-ID literals are rewritten
keep.src/lib/recruiting/live-pipeline.ts: PARKED, not moved and not deleted: open audit decision #1 (536 lines, 0 importers, and it writes synthetic applicants into real tables). If the decision is to keep it, its content says features/recruiting/api/ not domain/. Batch 10's gate is therefore 'src/lib contains exactly the files parked here' — the old tree cannot be deleted while a parked file is still in it.

moves._tier: shared infrastructure; the audit's rule 3 says it stays put and it never depends on a domain
risk: src/lib/db.ts:1 and src/lib/auth/client.ts:3 import from scripts/ (cross-boundary relatives)

moves._note: ai-guard.server.ts is largely pure (verifyEvidenceGrounding, normalizeForMatch) but keeps its .server suffix: the suffix is what the lint selector and ssrLoadModule read, and downgrading a suffix is a client/server change, not a move.

live-pipeline.ts is deliberately NOT moved here or anywhere: 0 importers and it writes synthetic applicants into real tables. It stays put until the open audit decision is answered; check-tree treats it as a keep.

Tier correction found by the Batch 1 rails, not by reading: batch.ts contains createServerFn handlers and lazily imports org.server, queue.server and parse.server. In the flat dir that was invisible; in domain/ it would have been a lint error, because domain is the isomorphic tier. Basename unchanged.

routes/api/queue/tick.ts stays (framework). observability.server.ts lazily imports queue.server.ts twice to break a cycle - that legal cycle is documented in 06:113-122 and the re-keyed rules must not fire on it.
polls every 2800ms, which is why networkidle never settles in QA

Four more api-tier-by-behaviour files that the flat naming hid: labels, portal, share and screen-session each contain createServerFn handlers and import .server modules, so domain/ would have been a lint error. Same reason check-tree asserts the tier from file content rather than from filename.

batch 3 (applied) gave the three folder-named modules real suffixes in place — harness/server.ts -> harness/harness.server.ts, harness/api.ts -> harness/harness-api.ts, benchmark/phases.ts -> benchmark/phases.server.ts — so they stopped evading the filename-based globs. These directory entries therefore carry the renamed files into src/features/eval unchanged. scripts/bench-live-arms.mjs:42 and benchmark-resume-match.mjs:48 import phases.server.ts by path.

origin.ts imports '@tanstack/react-start/server' — a framework package, not a local server module. It is the reason the client→server pattern list is anchored to ./ ../ and @/ specifiers instead of the bare '**/server' group the audit config first used.

api.ts moves whole with all 14 createServerFn export names unchanged (user decision). query.ts moves with it because query.ts:2 imports ./api - a client useQuery module sitting in the same flat dir as domain code; giving it the api tier is the honest answer and is what stops check-tree firing on arrival.
workspace-level surfaces that span ingest+ranking+people, same reasoning as the api hub.
net-new premium feature; created in its final home immediately after batch 1 so it exercises the re-keyed globs with production code and costs zero import rewrites.
